samples.summary: design-sandbox's vite `define` does not supply the new `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, so the Settings scene silently loses the new Offline section
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:193-197` defines `process.env`, `__APP_VERSION__` and `import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` — but not `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, which this change introduces in `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`. The sandbox aliases `@` → `packages/frontend/src` (vite.config.ts:219) and `scenes.config.json:215-233` registers the `settings-personal` scene against `packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx`, which now gates its whole Offline `<section>` on `supportsClientKey()`. `yorkie-capabilities.ts` guards with `typeof __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, so this degrades rather than crashing — it falls back to `'0.0.0'` and returns `false`. The sandbox's own comment at vite.config.ts:188-192 states the opposite intent ("Scene source IS real app source … an undefined global is a hard failure rather than a degraded render"). Today it happens to match production (the pin is 0.7.22), so the drift is invisible; the moment `@yorkie-js/react` is bumped to 0.7.23 the sandbox becomes the only place the section is missing, with nothing to signal it.

samples.summary: `useUnsavedWorkProbe` enumerates SyncState literally and was not updated for the new `saved-locally` member
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24` computes `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'not-saved' || state === 'saving';`. The `SyncState` union gained `'saved-locally'` in this change, and a document in that state has edits the server has not taken. Because the literal list was not extended, `registerUnsavedWorkProbe` is not registered, so `hasUnsavedWork()` answers `false` for it — which is what `lazy-with-retry.ts:158` and `:233` consult before letting the app reload itself. The same literal enumeration appears at `sync-status-chip.tsx` (`mayHaveUnsent = stranded || state === 'saving'`), which drives `useNavigationGuard`. This may well be deliberate (durable work survives a reload in the tab that owns the election), but nothing in the diff records the decision at this consumer, and a `Record<SyncState, …>` was updated two files over while this one was not — so the next state added here will silently miss it too.

samples.summary: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted unconditionally in `PrivateRoute`, bypassing the `supportsClientKey()` gate every other offline surface sits behind — it opens IndexedDB and issues an uncached full `GET /documents` on every authenticated page load of a build that can persist nothing
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/PrivateRoute.tsx:35` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` with no capability check, while `app/settings/page.tsx:35`, `sync-status-chip.tsx` (`offerOffline`) and `lib/use-durable-document.ts` (`eligibleNow`) all gate on `supportsClientKey()`, and `yorkie-capabilities.ts` documents that rule as "Every surface that offers the feature goes behind this, not only the code that performs it." On the pinned `@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22 (`packages/frontend/package.json:66`) `supportsClientKey()` is false, so nothing can ever be written — yet `OfflineRuntime`'s effect still constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening the IndexedDB database), runs `collectStale()`, and calls `fetchDocuments()`. That is a raw `fetchWithAuth` call, not a React Query, so it neither dedupes nor caches against the existing `['documents']` query; `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195` answers it with every document in every workspace the user belongs to, author metadata attached. One extra full-catalog query per authenticated session, for a feature that is dark.

samples.summary: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` treats `GET /documents` as an exhaustive list of everything the user may read, and deletes local archives — the only copy of unsent work — for anything absent from it
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx` passes `accessible.map((doc) => doc.id)` straight into `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`, whose implementation in `lib/offline-erase.ts` keeps only ids in that set and calls `purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", … })` for everything else. The contract it depends on lives in `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195`: `getDocuments` returns `listDocumentsWithAuthor({ where: { workspaceId: { in: workspaceIds } } })` with no take/skip, so the invariant holds today — access is membership and the listing is unpaginated. But nothing on either side records that dependency, and the failure is silent and unrecoverable in one direction: adding pagination, a `take`, or any per-document grant that is not a workspace membership would make the reconcile delete archived work the SDK could not reconcile, which by this feature's own design is the only durable copy. Worth a comment at the call site or an assertion that the response is complete, since the same endpoint is already consumed elsewhere as a plain list.
searchedFor: Checked schema.prisma Document.folder onDelete (SetNull — folder delete does not cascade)

samples.summary: The documented invariant "every `src` import of `@yorkie-js/sdk` is a type import" is now further out of date, and three new production modules import it while it is declared a devDependency
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/sync-status/use-sync-status.ts:23` states: "`@yorkie-js/sdk` is a devDependency here (every `src` import of it is a type import)". `packages/frontend/package.json:99` still lists it under `devDependencies`, and this change adds three production-path value imports: `src/lib/offline-copy.ts:1` (`import { Document }`), `src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts:1` (`import { Client, Document, Text }`), and a type-only one at `src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1` (`DocStore, StoredChange, StoredDoc`). The comment was already stale (`src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:1` imports `Client, Document` as values), so this is drift rather than a new break — but it now describes the opposite of what the tree does, in the one file a reader would consult about the boundary. Separately, the `DocStore`/`StoredChange`/`StoredDoc` type imports are erased at build and `packages/frontend` runs no `tsc`, so if the pinned 0.7.22 SDK does not export them, `WafflebaseDocStore implements DocStore` is vacuous and nothing anywhere would say so (I could not verify: node_modules is not present in this checkout).

finding.summary: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` treats `GET /documents` as an exhaustive list of everything the user may read, and deletes local archives — the only copy of unsent work — for anything absent from it
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx` passes `accessible.map((doc) => doc.id)` straight into `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`, whose implementation in `lib/offline-erase.ts` keeps only ids in that set and calls `purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", … })` for everything else. The contract it depends on lives in `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195`: `getDocuments` returns `listDocumentsWithAuthor({ where: { workspaceId: { in: workspaceIds } } })` with no take/skip, so the invariant holds today — access is membership and the listing is unpaginated. But nothing on either side records that dependency, and the failure is silent and unrecoverable in one direction: adding pagination, a `take`, or any per-document grant that is not a workspace membership would make the reconcile delete archived work the SDK could not reconcile, which by this feature's own design is the only durable copy. Worth a comment at the call site or an assertion that the response is complete, since the same endpoint is already consumed elsewhere as a plain list.
searchedFor: Checked schema.prisma Document.folder onDelete (SetNull — folder delete does not cascade)

verdict.reason: The mechanical claims check out (offline-runtime.tsx:154-160 passes the listed ids; offline-erase.ts:479-497 drops archives for everything outside the set), but there is no broken or bypassing site today, and the finding itself concedes this ("the invariant holds today"). GET /documents at document.controller.ts:180-195 has no take/skip/cursor (grep for take:|skip:|cursor: across packages/backend/src/document returns nothing), so the listing is exhaustive. The only non-membership read path in the schema (prisma/schema.prisma:153-168 ShareLink; no per-document grant model exists) cannot produce an offline archive at all, because the share route is wrapped in NonDurableScope (shared-document.tsx:1017, defined use-durable-document.ts:68-70) specifically to prevent a shared document from ever reaching the user's disk. The claim that "nothing on either side records that dependency" is also false: offline-runtime.tsx:142-153 and offline-erase.ts:432-435 both explicitly state that a partial listing must never reach the purge. What remains is a request for a defensive comment/assertion against a hypothetical future addition of pagination or per-document grants — latent-coupling documentation, which under this lens's rubric is at most minor doc-drift, not a major broken caller, guard bypass, or violated invariant read by another module.
